headline_marked: [[AMD Zen 7 EPYC CPUs]] split into 3 families for 2028
headline: AMD Zen 7 EPYC CPUs split into 3 families for 2028
summary: AMD's next-gen server processors, codenamed Florence, Ferrara, and Fidenza, will target distinct AI workloads starting in 2028.
details: AMD has revealed that its upcoming Zen 7 generation EPYC server CPUs, slated for release in 2028, will be divided into three distinct families: Florence, Ferrara, and Fidenza. This marks a departure from the unified approach seen in the Zen 5 generation.

Florence will feature new Zen 7 cores and AI compute extensions, with variants targeting both core performance and enterprise optimization. Ferrara is designed as an AI host node, while Fidenza is positioned as an "agentic sandbox" product for specialized AI deployments.

The company claims its sixth-gen EPYC processors enable the most AI agents per watt, per dollar, and per rack. However, these agent counts are estimated based on CPU thread resources and may vary with specific workloads and system configurations.

AMD's Helios rack-scale systems, featuring 72 Instinct MI455X GPUs and 18 Venice CPUs, are now in production. These systems are claimed to offer up to 30% more inference tokens per dollar compared to Nvidia's Vera Rubin NVL72.

The fourth-gen EPYC (Zen 4) had multiple families like Genoa and Bergamo, while the fifth-gen (Zen 5) consolidated into a single stack. The Zen 7 lineup with three named families represents a wider initial spread for a generation than AMD has previously launched.

headline_marked: [[InteraOne]]: Open-source AI assistant for product integration
headline: InteraOne: Open-source AI assistant for product integration
summary: A new open-source infrastructure aims to make embedding AI-powered customer interactions into web applications seamless for developers.
details: InteraOne is an open-source AI assistant designed to be embedded directly into web applications, offering an alternative to traditional customer support widgets.

The platform provides developers with an infrastructure for building AI-powered customer interactions, aiming to simplify the process of integrating chat UIs, AI orchestration, knowledge retrieval, and conversation management.
Unlike closed-source solutions, InteraOne emphasizes developer ownership and extensibility, allowing for inspection, modification, and self-hosting of the underlying infrastructure.
The vision is to create an open-source AI interaction layer for modern web applications, evolving from AI support agents to product assistants and automated workflows.
The project welcomes contributions and ideas from developers interested in AI infrastructure, agents, RAG, real-time systems, and developer tooling.
caption:
Building an open-source alternative to Intercom's AI assistant. InteraOne aims to make AI integration trivial for developers.

InteraOne is an open-source AI assistant designed to be embedded directly into web applications, offering an alternative to traditional customer support widgets.

The platform provides developers with an infrastructure for building AI-powered customer interactions, aiming to simplify the process of integrating chat UIs, AI orchestration, knowledge retrieval, and conversation management.

Unlike closed-source solutions, InteraOne emphasizes developer ownership and extensibility, allowing for inspection, modification, and self-hosting of the underlying infrastructure.

The vision is to create an open-source AI interaction layer for modern web applications, evolving from AI support agents to product assistants and automated workflows.

The project welcomes contributions and ideas from developers interested in AI infrastructure, agents, RAG, real-time systems, and developer tooling.
